title: Energy flow in a grassland reserve

stimulus.title: Producer data for a grassland reserve

table.caption: Measurements for the producers of a 3 km² grassland reserve (invented data for practice). 1 km² = 1,000,000 m².
rows: Energy used by the producers in respiration (R)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the net primary productivity (NPP) of the grassland. Show your work and include units.

rubric.point: A correct setup: GPP minus respiration, with the values substituted
The correct answer with units: 10,000 kcal/m²/yr
accept: 10,000 kcal per square meter per year

parts.sample: NPP = GPP - R = 25,000 kcal/m²/yr - 15,000 kcal/m²/yr = 10,000 kcal/m²/yr.

mistakes.why: NPP is what is left after respiration: subtract R from GPP.
You added GPP and R. NPP = GPP - R.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using your answer to part (a) and the 10% rule, calculate the energy available to the meadowlarks. Show your work and include units.

rubric.point: A correct setup: NPP times 0.10 for each of two steps (grasses to grasshoppers to meadowlarks)
The correct answer with units: 100 kcal/m²/yr (or consistent with an incorrect part (a))
accept: 100 kcal per square meter per year

parts.sample: Meadowlarks are secondary consumers, two steps above the producers: 10,000 kcal/m²/yr × 0.10 × 0.10 = 100 kcal/m²/yr.

mistakes.why: That is three steps, which reaches the hawks. Meadowlarks are two steps above the grasses.
Start from NPP (10,000), the energy actually available to consumers, not GPP.
You applied the 10% rule three times. Grasses to meadowlarks is two steps.
You started from GPP. Use NPP, 10,000 kcal/m²/yr.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the total energy available to the meadowlarks in the whole 3 km² reserve each year. Show your work and include units.

rubric.point: A correct setup that converts km² to m² and multiplies by the energy per m² from part (b)
The correct answer with units: 3 × 10⁸ kcal/yr (or consistent with part (b))

mistakes.why: You left the area in km². Convert 3 km² to 3,000,000 m² before multiplying by kcal per m².
That is one square kilometer. The reserve is 3 km², so multiply by 3 as well.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why only about 10% of the energy in the grasshoppers is available to the meadowlarks.

rubric.point: Most energy is used by the grasshoppers for cellular respiration (movement, growth, body heat) and released as heat
accept: energy is lost as heat in respiration
the second law of thermodynamics: each transfer releases heat

rubric.point: Some energy is never passed on: parts are not eaten or not digested and leave as waste, going to decomposers
accept: not all of the grasshopper is eaten

parts.sample: Grasshoppers use most of the energy they take in for cellular respiration to move, grow and stay alive, and that energy is released as heat, which meadowlarks cannot use. Also, some grasshoppers are never eaten, and some of what is eaten is not digested and leaves as waste, so its energy goes to decomposers instead.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A rancher proposes removing the hawks from the reserve. Describe the most likely effect on the meadowlark population, and explain one effect this could have on the grasshoppers.

rubric.point: Meadowlarks increase, because fewer are eaten by hawks
accept: the meadowlark population grows with fewer predators

rubric.point: Grasshoppers decrease, because more meadowlarks eat more grasshoppers
accept: more grasshoppers are eaten, so their population falls

parts.sample: Without hawks, fewer meadowlarks are killed by predators, so the meadowlark population increases. With more meadowlarks feeding, more grasshoppers are eaten, so the grasshopper population decreases.
